clue.text: Ran low, went in, refuelled

indicators.note: the word low is said to have gone into the other piece, so it sits inside it

parts.note: to refuel a body is to feed it, so refuelled gives fed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tank or a driver ran low on fuel, pulled into a station and filled up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran low' looks like one phrase, but 'Ran' alone is the definition and 'low' is the piece that goes inside FED.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that ran along a channel moved steadily in a stream, the past tense of flow.

clue.text: Broken limb mended, went to sea

definitions.meaning: once a broken limb has healed, the plaster cast comes off
a boat that set sail untied its mooring ropes and left port

explanation.surface: A sailor whose broken leg has healed heads back to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the plaster when a break has mended, and untying a ship's lines to sail, are both described by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Rolling Stone following pretty girl is criminal!

indicators.note: the jumbled stone comes after the slang word for a pretty girl

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: rolling means the letters of stone tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A member of the Rolling Stones chasing a pretty girl is up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' reads as the band member, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal: STONE becomes ONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal and its synonym both describe conduct that is crooked, deceitful or untrustworthy.

clue.text: Finding the wrong tag round has horrified

indicators.note: the jumbled tag is wrapped round the word has
wrong signals that the letters of tag are put into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discovering that a price label is incorrect has shocked someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes AGT from the label word, and 'round' wraps that around the verb taken as written. 'Finding the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone horrified is struck with shock and dismay, which is exactly what this word describes.

clue.text: A foreign coin collection housed in the plant

indicators.note: housed in says one piece is lodged inside the other

parts.note: the pea is a climbing garden plant
a set is a collection of things that go together

explanation.surface: A coin collector keeps their foreign coins hidden in a potted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency unit of Spain before the euro, so it is a foreign coin to a British solver.

clue.text: A sight in the hat with the gold lining!

indicators.note: the gold is a lining, sitting inside the hat

parts.note: a panama is a lightweight straw hat
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone in a hat lined with gold is quite a sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lining' signals the insertion. Gold as OR comes from heraldry, the language of coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide view of a landscape is a sight to take in, and this word names such a sweeping view.

clue.text: Written by the Fortes, it's a hard back

indicators.note: written by places the musical marks right beside the reversed letters
back says those letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the word it's, apostrophe ignored, gives the letters i, t, s
forte is marked f in music, so two of them give ff

explanation.surface: A book by the Forte family turns out to be a hardback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ITS to STI. 'Fortes' are the music sign f, loud, so two give FF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid that will not bend is hard to the touch, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Exchange rate above certain value

indicators.note: in a down entry, above puts the jumbled letters first
exchange means the letters of rate swap places

parts.note: taken as written
to be certain is to be sure

explanation.surface: A currency exchange rate is higher than some fixed value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange rate' reads as a finance term, but 'Exchange' is the anagram signal turning RATE into TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something highly is to cherish it, the verb sense of a word also meaning hoard of riches.

clue.text: The remainder of the departures

definitions.meaning: what is left over, such as scraps at the end of a meal
acts of going away from a place

explanation.surface: Whatever is left over from the people heading off.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both leftover scraps and occasions of people going away.

clue.text: Since wrongly carrying the article, get urges

indicators.note: the jumbled letters carry the other piece inside them
wrongly says the letters of since are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
it is the pronoun for the thing or article in question

explanation.surface: Having mistakenly lugged an item around, someone feels compulsions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' gives INCES, and 'carrying' takes the article inside it. 'urges' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to stir or provoke them into action, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: See and set free what got caught in

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes in among the rearranged letters
letters set free scatter, so the word what is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Look, and release whatever got snared in the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' gives WATH, and 'in' puts the cricket C among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a match or show is to look on as an observer, a common verb synonym.

clue.text: Is the water in which it swims fenced in?

definitions.text: Is the water in which it swims fenced in?

parts.words: Is the water in which it swims fenced in?
parts.note: a creature named for a fencing weapon might be imagined to fence, so its water would be fenced

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fish's pond has a fence around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fenced' means enclosed on the surface but swordplay in the cryptic reading: this fish carries a blade-like bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish has a long sword-like bill, so it is the swimmer whose water you could call fenced.

clue.text: 'Fatuous' is not fair

definitions.meaning: feeble and silly, the British sense of a drip or weakling
fair weather is dry, so weather that is not fair is rainy

explanation.surface: Calling something fatuous is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a feeble, ineffectual person is called this, and the same word describes rainy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both feebly silly and rainy, the opposite of fair weather.

clue.text: Sure as to which article it is

definitions.text: as to which article it is
definitions.meaning: grammar names the article the as one kind, the other kind being a or an

explanation.surface: Someone is confident about which item a thing is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' reads as an item, but it is the grammar term: the word the is called this kind of article.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure means being certain, and the grammar label for the article the uses the same word.

clue.text: Tender lovers

parts.note: tender here is money, as in legal tender, so these are people who love money

explanation.surface: Gentle, affectionate romantic partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective meaning gentle; it is the noun, money.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarders who love cash above all are lovers of legal tender.

clue.text: In which the makers of innovations are listed?

definitions.text: In which the makers of innovations are listed?

parts.words: In which the makers of innovations are listed?
parts.note: makers of innovations are inventors, and a list of them sounds like a register of inventors

explanation.surface: A question about the directory that records who invented what.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is read playfully as a place for inventors, as if it were a dormitory or repository, though it really means a list of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: This word is a complete itemised list, and its spelling suggests a register for inventors.

clue.text: The tailless dog does recover

indicators.note: tailless means the dog's final letter is cut off

parts.note: a retriever is a gundog breed

explanation.surface: A dog with no tail still manages to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' removes the last letter of the dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover lost property is to get it back, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: An afterthought: 'Back in spring'

indicators.note: back says the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving a
a PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A letter's postscript adds: 'Back in spring', announcing a return date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses A PS to SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral spring, whose waters people visit for health, is called by this name.

clue.text: Through loans, contrived to get one's own

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post

indicators.note: contrived means the letters of loans are artfully rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: By borrowing money, someone schemes to acquire property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' turns LOANS into SONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to oneself and no other person is private or individual.

clue.text: Beat, but not black and blue

definitions.meaning: to thrash, as in tanning someone's hide
a light brown colour, rather than the dark shades of a bruise

explanation.surface: Someone was thrashed but somehow left unbruised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black and blue' reads as bruised, but it names colours: a light brown is neither.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to thrash someone and a yellowish-brown colour.

clue.text: Far be it from me to switch on again!

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again, as in redo

indicators.note: switch means the letters of me to change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares they would never turn the device on again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' is the anagram signal. The answer is also the hand-held gadget for switching a television on, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant place is far away, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Bother to put notice by hole

indicators.note: by puts the two pieces side by side

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
the letter o is round like a hole

explanation.surface: Someone can't be bothered to stick an advert next to a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and trouble, as in much fuss about nothing, is what this short word means.

clue.text: So to squash racket, became a deputy

indicators.note: squash means the letters of so to are crushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a din is a loud racket or noise

explanation.surface: Someone went to play squash, rackets in hand, as a substitute player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash racket' reads as sports kit, but 'squash' is the anagram signal (SO TO gives STOO) and 'racket' is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill in for an absent person is to act as a deputy or substitute, a phrasal verb in the past.

clue.text: Evicted day before, is gloomy

indicators.note: before says the abbreviation for day comes first

parts.note: a tenant who is evicted is thrown out, or ejected

explanation.surface: Thrown out of their home the day before, someone is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being downcast and low in spirits is the same as feeling gloomy.

clue.text: And what have you against the female artist?

indicators.note: against means touching, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on, or and what have you
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone asks what else you hold against the woman painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what have you' reads as a question, but it is the phrase meaning et cetera.
explanation.definitionFit: A printmaker who engraves designs on metal plates with acid is an artist of this kind.

clue.text: And upset by his bad language

indicators.note: by puts the two jumbled pieces side by side
upset means the letters of and are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bad means the letters of his are badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is offended by a man's foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AND into DAN and 'bad' turns HIS into ISH. 'bad language' looks like swearing, but only 'language' is the definition.

clue.text: Marksman's two attempts

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, as in have a crack at it
a shot is an attempt, as in give it a shot

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter gets two goes at the target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two attempts' supplies both halves: two different words for a try.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert shot who rarely misses is a marksman, so the phrase fits exactly.

clue.text: Animal I caught hiding within plants

indicators.note: hiding within says the letter for caught is tucked inside the animal

parts.note: a cat is an animal
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An animal I caught was hiding among some plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding within' puts C inside CAT to make CACT, then I is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny succulents of the desert are a family of plants, and this is the plural form.

clue.text: It's sharp and ripped a little hole in it

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the word for ripped

parts.note: something ripped is torn

indicators.note: a little of the word hole is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A sharp object tore a small hole in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little hole' is just H, the first letter of hole, and 'in' puts it inside TORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike on a rose stem is pointed and sharp enough to prick skin.

clue.text: In the carved base, opposed concealed lights

indicators.note: the jumbled letters conceal the other piece inside them
carved means the letters of base are cut and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
con is short for contra, the argument against

explanation.surface: Hidden lights are set into a carved pedestal, against someone's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' gives BEAS and 'concealed' signals the insertion. Opposed is CON, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal fires and lighthouses that guide or warn are lights of this kind.

clue.text: Doesn't do to have recurrent themes

definitions.meaning: holds back from doing something, abstains
repeated choruses or lines in a song or poem

explanation.surface: Someone avoids using repeated motifs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for abstaining and a plural noun for repeated choruses in music.

clue.text: Take rifle out to lake for another shot

indicators.note: out means the letters of rifle are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
l is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A hunter takes their gun down to the lake to have another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as a gunshot, but the definition means another drink poured, or a top-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up of a glass is another serving, and a shot is a small measure of drink.
